scope: Proposition 6.12 (Products of bounded types) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 47. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For bounded types p(x), q(y) over A, realize p in an extension B ≥ A and then realize qB in a further extension. The joint type of (x, y) over A, denoted p ⊗ q, is independent of all choices. Binary products are symmetric, with the indicated permutation of coordinates. Finite products associate, are permutation invariant, and commute with coordinate projections. Furthermore (p ⊗ q)B = pB ⊗ qB . (4) These assertions hold across eligible levels when all originating arities and uniform testing costs are bounded at the smallest level. If x/B is free from A and x, d have product type over B, then x and (d, e) have product type over A for every bounded tuple e from B.
